title: Correct streaming disconnect accounting (stop billing after client disconnect; capture partial usage)
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Fixes overcounting of streaming output tokens after client disconnect; adds explicit disconnect outcome + tests; includes backfill tooling + runbook notes.
body: Context: We found that a subset of streaming requests were being metered beyond the point of client disconnect. Root cause was that the streaming loop continued to enqueue/compress tokens after the client transport closed, and the metering hook used the model-emitted token counter rather than the bytes successfully sent (and it was invoked after the cancellation signal in some paths). This manifested as invoice > console usage for customers with frequent disconnects/timeouts (see SUP-3160) and showed up in reconciliation samples as a right-tail of deltas on streaming-heavy workloads. Change summary: (1) Stop counting billable output tokens after client disconnect by wiring request cancellation (client connection close / HTTP2 reset / websocket close) into the stream emitter and metering hook; once cancellation is observed we finalize the meter for tokens already emitted and prevent any subsequent increments. (2) Ensure partial usage is captured by snapshotting token counts per chunk prior to write/flush, and emitting a final meter event on disconnect with request_outcome=client_disconnect and streamed_output_tokens equal to tokens actually emitted before cancellation. (3) Add explicit dimensions so Finance/Support can explain differences: request_outcome includes success | client_disconnect | server_error | timeout, and streaming_finish_reason includes stop | length | client_disconnect | error. (4) Add regression tests covering: disconnect mid-stream, disconnect during first chunk, retries that re-open a stream, and server-side cancellation. Implementation notes: - We now subscribe to the transport close signal and propagate it through the streaming context (StreamContext.cancelled()). - Metering increments happen only on successful chunk encode, and the finalization event uses the last committed counter rather than the model internal counter. - We guard against double-finalization by making finalize() idempotent (atomic compare-and-set) and by ensuring the metering middleware does not emit an end event if the stream emitter already did. Backfill notes: This PR includes a one-off backfill job entrypoint (tools/metering/backfill_streaming_disconnects.py) that recomputes streaming_output_tokens for a specified time window from raw chunk logs and overwrites the billing aggregate rows for that window (writes a new aggregation_window_id and invoice_run_id tag for audit). Proposed window: 2026-01-15 through 2026-02-03 (matches period implicated in reconciliation sample B + SUP-3160). Backfill must be run only after Finance sign-off and prior to invoice finalization; output artifacts: per-account delta CSV, before/after aggregate parquet, and a summary markdown for close evidence. Risk/rollout: Low risk to non-streaming endpoints; streaming paths only. Rollout behind flag streaming_metering_strict_disconnect (default on in staging, canary in prod to 5% of orgs for 24h). Observability: Added metric metering.streaming.disconnect_finalized_total and a counter for post-cancel increment attempts (should be 0). Test plan: - Unit tests for StreamTokenAccumulator finalize semantics. - Integration tests using a simulated client that disconnects after N chunks. - Manual: replay sample requests from SUP-3160 logs in staging and verify billed tokens == console tokens within documented rounding tolerance. Checklist: [x] Added tests [x] Updated runbook note in docs/billing/metering_edge_cases.md [x] Added dashboard metric for disconnect finalizations [x] Verified no change to non-streaming meters. Notes for Support/Finance: After this change, invoices should no longer include tokens generated after the connection closes. Customers may still see small differences between console and invoice due to time zone cutoffs and rounding (handled in ADR-027), but disconnect-related overage should be eliminated.
commits: metering(streaming): finalize output token counter on client disconnect
gateway: propagate transport close into StreamContext cancellation
tests(streaming): regression coverage for mid-stream disconnect + retry paths
tools: add backfill job for streaming disconnect accounting + audit artifacts
conversation: Logan Wright (review): The core fix makes sense. Two questions: (1) Are we sure we’re not undercounting tokens that were generated but never flushed? (2) Can we guarantee finalize() fires in all disconnect paths (HTTP2 reset vs websocket close)?

Nadia Rahman (author): (1) Intentional: billing should reflect tokens emitted to the client prior to disconnect. Previously we effectively billed generated tokens even if they never left the server. We now increment only on successful chunk encode and commit before flush. (2) Yes; StreamContext listens to both response 'close' and underlying transport reset where available; added integration tests for both ws close and HTTP2 reset simulation.

Cole Summers (review): Please ensure metering middleware doesn’t emit a second end-of-request meter event when the stream emitter has already finalized on disconnect. Also, can we add invoice_run_id tagging to backfill writes to keep auditability?
Nadia Rahman (author): Added an atomic finalized flag + middleware guard. Backfill writer now requires invoice_run_id and writes aggregation_window_id + meter_version; included in tool README.
Allison Grant (review): Can we add an alert if post-cancel increments happen? That would catch regressions quickly, and also help during backfill/replay where we might see noise.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added metering.streaming.post_cancel_increment_attempt_total with a 0-threshold alert in prod (5m, >=1) and a suppression rule for backfill job labels; see dashboard change.

Emily Stone (Finance) (comment): For backfill: we need a per-account delta report and a sign-off step before anything writes to billing aggregates. Please reference the close checklist item and output location.

Nadia Rahman (author): Backfill tool now outputs (a) per-account deltas CSV, (b) summary md, (c) before/after aggregates to GCS path gs://redwood-finance-audit/metering_backfills/<invoice_run_id>/, and it refuses to run without --finance_approved_by and --ticket (Linear/Jira) flags. Added a note in tools README with the close checklist link.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Thanks for tightening the semantics and adding tests/metrics.
Cole Summers (approval): Approved after latest changes.
Emily Stone (approval): Approved contingent on running backfill only after Finance sign-off (captured in tool).
